result.title: AIRIS: Benchmarking Social Embodied Intelligence in Egocentric Streaming Videos
result.summary: Embodied agents operating around people must not only recognize social cues, but also decide when the available evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without violating social norms. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these abilities in isolation or with access to completed videos, obscuring where an online social decision fails. We introduce AIRIS, a causal streaming benchmark that formulates social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored chain of Attention, Intention, Reaction, and Interaction (A-I-R-I). AIRIS contains 8,000 expert-curated questions grounded in 357 egocentric clips across 11 context categories and 36 capability dimensions. At each query, models receive only the observation prefix available at that time; decision-aware metrics reward calibrated waiting and complete reactions while penalizing premature commitment. Evaluating 45 proprietary and open-source general-purpose, embodied, streaming-video, and omni-modal models reveals fragmented and temporally miscalibrated competence. General-purpose VLMs excel at passive cue grounding and intent recognition, whereas embodied specialists lead on isolated reaction sub-decisions; yet across all families, models frequently guess intents before sufficient evidence emerges and fail to jointly align intervention timing, action domain, and concrete execution within the same episode. AIRIS thus provides a diagnostic foundation for bridging the gap between passive social perception and reliable embodied interaction.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AIRIS，一个基于第一人称流式视频的因果基准，将社交具身智能拆为 Attention–Intention–Reaction–Interaction 的时间锚定链条，含 357 个片段、8,000 道题；模型每次只看到当下可得的观察前缀，并用决策感知指标奖励校准的等待、惩罚过早承诺，据此评测 45 个模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据是否充分、何时等待或介入」的评测设计与 LVR 的 STOP 决策、证据筛选和过早承诺问题直接相关，普遍出现的「证据未现即猜意图」失败模式可供核查 latent 推理中的提前收敛；但对象是社交具身任务，不涉及 latent 状态生成机制。
